title: Plain-language public explainer (what RideBelt is and is not)
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. Visitors need a short, honest page: the problem, the idea, the open-standard approach, and above all that it is NOT ready or approved for use.
objective: Write a 600–900 word explainer at about an 8th-grade reading level, following the messaging rules in docs/business/stakeholders.md.
acceptanceCriteria: Leads with the safety notice; makes no claim that it prevents deaths
States what it cannot help with (structural failure, collisions)
Readability at or below grade 9 (state the tool used)
